title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BUTTERFINGERS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Wendell Bixby, a diner cook in Lake Charles, Louisiana.
Wendell can flip an egg without breaking the yolk. Everything else? He drops it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BIG DROP
segments.quote: Taking a new step, uttering a new word, is what people fear most.
segments.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
lines: One Sunday rush, Wendell dropped a tray of twelve plates. Grits on the ceiling.
The waitress, Darla, named him Butterfingers. By lunch, the whole town knew.
That night, his wife Tonya's Crime and Punishment lay open on the nightstand:
Taking a new step, uttering a new word, is what people fear most.
Next day, Wendell bought three juggling balls at the dollar store.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TWO HUNDRED DROPS
segments.quote: Life is short, and Art long; the crisis fleeting; experience perilous, and decision difficult.
segments.author: Hippocrates
lines: Night one, the balls went under the couch and, once, into the cat.
Tonya, a nurse, had a line in her locker from Hippocrates, the old Greek doctor:
Life is short, and Art long; the crisis fleeting; experience perilous, and decision difficult.
Translation: you'll never feel ready, so start now.
He practiced every break, out back by the dumpster.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE REGULARS
segments.quote: Cheerfulness keeps up a kind of daylight in the mind, and fills it with a steady and perpetual serenity.
segments.author: Joseph Addison
lines: The regulars watched through the back window and laughed.
He almost hid. Then he read the old sign over the register, from Joseph Addison, an English writer:
Cheerfulness keeps up a kind of daylight in the mind, and fills it with a steady and perpetual serenity.
So every time he dropped one, he took a bow. By Friday, they were clapping.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE THROW
segments.quote: The problem with juggling is that the balls go where you throw them.
segments.author: Ronald Graham
lines: But he still chased the balls all over the parking lot.
Miss Ruby, an old circus juggler, quoted Ronald Graham, a math professor who juggled:
The problem with juggling is that the balls go where you throw them.
Fix the throw, she said, and the catch takes care of itself.
Soon, three balls stayed up a whole minute.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BIG TALK
segments.quote: Do not count your chickens before they are hatched.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: Then Wendell got cocky. He swore he'd juggle a frying pan at Miss June's eightieth birthday.
Darla slid an egg across the counter and quoted Aesop:
Do not count your chickens before they are hatched.
He tried the frying pan once. Dented the cooler. Back to three.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE PARTY
segments.quote: Just to keep alive isn't enough. To live you must have sunshine and freedom and a little flower to love!
segments.author: Hans Christian Andersen
lines: At the party, one orange landed in the gravy. He bowed. Big cheer.
Then he juggled an egg, cracked it on the griddle, and served Miss June her birthday egg.
Miss June laughed till she cried, and read from her Hans Christian Andersen book:
Just to keep alive isn't enough. To live you must have sunshine and freedom and a little flower to love!
Now Wendell juggles every Saturday, and the diner is packed.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Take the step. Start now. Smile at drops. Fix the throw. Stay humble. Bring sunshine.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Take the step. Start now. Smile at drops. Fix the throw. Stay humble. Bring sunshine.
I tried juggling once. My ceiling has three dents and my lamp is very nervous.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
